name: Nuclear plant safety
value: ZNPP lost all off-site power on 8 Nov
summary: Zaporizhzhia lost all off-site power on 8 Nov for the 27th time; on diesel generators with about two weeks' fuel
state: Zaporizhzhia lost its last external line, Ferosplavna-1, early on 8 Nov, the 27th total loss of off-site power of the war, and is running on emergency diesel generators with fuel for about two weeks, the IAEA said; the cause and location are not yet known (Anadolu). The plant's Russian-installed management reported normal radiation levels (Reuters via Internazionale). IAEA Director General Grossi described a continued precarious nuclear safety situation. No damage to safety systems or radiological release had been reported as of 8 Nov.
for_you: Radiation levels were reported normal. The exposure is local to the plant area and depends on how soon grid power returns before generator fuel runs down.
rubric_hit: Plant lost all off-site power on 8 Nov (Watch line); no safety-system damage, INES 2+ event or release reported for Alert

sources.title: Anadolu — Zaporizhzhya nuclear plant loses all external power for 27th time
Reuters via Internazionale — Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant relying on generators again after losing external power supply

why: Fighting near nuclear power plants risks a radiological release; the IAEA reports on Zaporizhzhia and other plants in or near war zones.
drivers: Off-site power losses, strikes near plants, staffing, cooling water, military occupation.

rubric.alert: Damage to safety-critical systems, an INES level 2 or higher event, or a radiological release.
rubric.watch: A plant loses all off-site power, strikes land near a plant, or the IAEA reports a deteriorating safety situation.
rubric.normal: No new IAEA safety concerns at plants in or near conflict zones.
